result.instructions: Tools for TimeHunter, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Who is working right now, and who is on a break?"; "How many hours did one employee work this month, and how much overtime do they have?"; "Show the attendance for the whole team yesterday.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes TimeHunter data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run timehunter_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run timehunter_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run timehunter_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. timehunter_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: timehunter_employee_status
tools.title: Employee status now
tools.description: List every employee with their current work state: working, on break, and the start time of today's session. Good first call to get employee ids. TimeHunter API: GET /api/employees/status.

tools.name: timehunter_get_work_time_today
tools.title: Work time today
tools.description: Get one employee's net working time today in seconds (totalSeconds) and the number of work sessions. TimeHunter API: GET /api/work/today.

tools.name: timehunter_list_attendance
tools.title: List attendance
tools.description: List attendance per employee and day: check-in, check-out, break times, work time and location. Defaults to today. Give date, or date_from and date_to together. TimeHunter API: GET /api/attendance.

date_from.description: First day of a range (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with date_to.

date_to.description: Last day of a range (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with date_from.

employee_id.description: Employee id (UUID). Omit for all employees.

tools.name: timehunter_get_daily_report
tools.title: Daily report
tools.description: Get one employee's report for today: net work seconds and each work session with start, end and break times. The API always reports today and ignores other dates. TimeHunter API: GET /api/report/daily.

tools.name: timehunter_get_weekly_report
tools.title: Weekly report
tools.description: Get one employee's work seconds per day for the current week (dailyTotals). TimeHunter API: GET /api/report/weekly.

tools.name: timehunter_get_monthly_report
tools.title: Monthly report
tools.description: Get one employee's work seconds per day for a month (dailyTotals, days with work only). Defaults to the current month. TimeHunter API: GET /api/report/monthly.

tools.name: timehunter_get_period_summary
tools.title: Period summary
tools.description: Get a summary per employee and month: work hours, norm, overtime, balance, late arrivals, absence days by type, and weekend or holiday work. Defaults to the previous and current month. TimeHunter API: GET /api/report/summary.

date_from.description: Start of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with date_to instead of months.

date_to.description: End of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Use with date_from instead of months.

employees.description: Comma-separated employee names or UUIDs. Omit for all active employees.

detail.description: true adds one row per day (in/out, lateness, day type).

tools.name: timehunter_list_schedules
tools.title: List schedules
tools.description: List work schedules for one month: each day's planned start and end, and the actual presence (arrival, departure, session id). TimeHunter API: GET /api/schedules.

employee_ids.description: Comma-separated employee UUIDs. Omit for all employees.
